title: Spin disorder competing with positional symmetry breaking governs the metal-insulator behavior in oxide paramagnets
summary: Numerous transition-metal oxides have low-temperature, long-range-ordered antiferromagnetic (AFM) states that are generally insulating, and high-temperature, disordered paramagnetic (PM) phases. The latter can be either insulating (predicted here for NaFeO3), or metallic (predicted here and previously observed in NaOsO3). Similar distinctions have been traditionally affected in strongly correlated models by the value used for Coulomb repulsion U.
